title: NVIDIA BlueField-4 STX Server for CMX at OCP 2026
gist: At OCP 2026 partners showed a cost-reduced NVIDIA BlueField-4 STX board for Context Memory (CMX): a single soldered Vera CPU with SOCAMM/LPDDR5X instead of the earlier dual-Vera plus four ConnectX-9 design. ServeTheHome argues BlueField-4 is really a single-socket server rather than a DPU, and that the cheaper bill of materials matters because rising NAND prices are inflating CMX storage system costs.

insights.claim: NVIDIA built a lower-cost BlueField-4 STX board for Context Memory (CMX) using a single Vera CPU after partners asked for it, replacing the earlier dual-Vera design with four ConnectX-9 SuperNICs.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is responding to partner cost pressure on KV-cache/context-memory storage nodes.
insights.quote: Partners had been asking for this, and NVIDIA delivered.

insights.claim: Moving from dual Vera to single Vera makes STX/CMX a cheaper platform, which should help these systems reach market while NAND prices have risen meaningfully over the past year.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Rising NAND costs squeeze context-memory storage budgets, so compute BOM cuts become the lever for adoption.
insights.quote: that will likely help the STX/ CMX systems come to market as the price of NAND has been rising meaningfully over the past year

insights.claim: No ConnectX-9 SuperNIC was seen on the BlueField-4 STX boards shown at OCP 2026, contrary to ServeTheHome's expectation.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Networking attach per CMX node may be lower or decoupled from the board, a possible cost lever and a watch item for NIC volume.
insights.quote: We expected that, but did not see it on this board.

themes.theme: BlueField-4 is a server, not a DPU

insights.claim: The BlueField-4 'DPU' carries a full Vera-class CPU and is effectively a high-end single-socket server platform, not an embedded-class DPU like BlueField-1 or BlueField-3.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: NVIDIA's DPU label understates how much server CPU silicon and ASP it is shipping into storage nodes.
insights.quote: This is more like having a high-end single-socket server platform.

insights.claim: For storage-platform builders, the original dual-Vera BlueField-4 is closer to a dual-CPU server than a traditional DPU in cost terms.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: NVIDIA competes for the storage-server CPU socket, not just the NIC/DPU slot.
insights.quote: the below is more akin to a dual CPU server than a traditional DPU

insights.claim: ServeTheHome suggests NVIDIA needs a separate brand between its Vera server line and the traditional BlueField DPU line, as the product category is blurring.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Product taxonomy confusion signals NVIDIA's expansion into general-purpose CPU platforms under networking branding.
insights.quote: It almost feels like NVIDIA needs some brand between the Vera server line and the traditional BlueField DPU line.

insights.claim: Soldered CPU and LPDDR5X instead of DDR5 DIMM slots shrink the BlueField-4 STX 'motherboard' to roughly the footprint of a single Intel DMR or AMD EPYC Venice 16-channel socket.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Density advantage versus x86 storage servers, at the cost of memory serviceability/configurability.
insights.locator: Something that may not immediately hit

insights.claim: The STX boards use SOCAMM memory, making it relatively easy to fit either an air heatsink or a liquid cooling block.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Supports liquid-cooled deployment of storage/context nodes alongside AI racks.

insights.claim: NVIDIA appears to have designed the STX board for easy automated assembly rather than as a traditional motherboard replacement.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Points to high-volume, hyperscale-style manufacturing intent for CMX nodes.
insights.quote: NVIDIA designed this less like a traditional motherboard replacement and more like something that is easy to assemble automatically

insights.claim: The board includes an M.2 slot, which beyond OS boot could serve as a log device, as ServeTheHome saw M.2 SSDs used in AWS's networking lab.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Small onboard flash roles add incremental SSD attach in AI infrastructure.
